xslg.name: Expected Slugging (xSLG)
xslg.definition: How many total bases a hitter is expected to get per at-bat, based on how hard and at what angle the ball was hit. It strips out luck and defense.

brl_percent.name: Barrel Rate
brl_percent.definition: A barrel is a batted ball with an ideal combination of exit velocity and launch angle. Barrel Rate is how often a hitter makes that kind of high-quality contact.

hard_hit_percent.name: Hard-Hit Rate
hard_hit_percent.definition: Percentage of batted balls hit at 95 mph or higher. It shows how often a hitter makes hard contact with the ball.

xba.name: Expected Batting Average (xBA)
xba.definition: The batting average a player should have based on the quality of contact (exit velocity, launch angle, sprint speed), rather than the actual result of each ball in play.

xwoba.name: Expected wOBA
xwoba.definition: Expected weighted on-base average. A single number for overall offensive value that credits walks, singles and extra-base hits by how much they are worth, estimated from contact quality.

squared_up_rate.name: Squared-Up Rate
squared_up_rate.definition: How often a swing produces close to the maximum possible exit velocity for that bat speed and pitch speed. Higher means cleaner contact.

chase_percent.name: Chase Rate
chase_percent.definition: Percentage of pitches outside the strike zone that the hitter swings at. For hitters, lower is better. For pitchers it is flipped: a higher chase rate means they fool hitters more often.

k_percent.name: Strikeout Rate (K%)
k_percent.definition: Strikeouts divided by plate appearances. For hitters, lower is better. For pitchers, higher is better.

bb_percent.name: Walk Rate (BB%)
bb_percent.definition: Walks divided by plate appearances. For hitters, higher is better. For pitchers, lower is better.

whiff_percent.name: Whiff Rate
whiff_percent.definition: Percentage of swings that miss the ball entirely. For hitters, lower is better. For pitchers, higher is better.

bat_speed.name: Bat Speed
bat_speed.definition: Average speed of the sweet spot of the bat at contact. Faster swings produce harder-hit balls.

exit_velocity.name: Average Exit Velocity
exit_velocity.definition: The average speed of the ball right after it leaves the bat. For pitchers, a lower value means they are limiting hard contact.

xera.name: Expected ERA (xERA)
xera.definition: What a pitcher's ERA should be based on the quality of contact allowed, strikeouts and walks, rather than the runs that actually scored.

era.name: Earned Run Average (ERA)
era.definition: Earned runs allowed per nine innings pitched. The classic bottom-line pitching stat. Lower is better.

whip.name: WHIP
whip.definition: Walks And Hits per Inning Pitched. It shows how well a pitcher keeps runners off the bases: walks plus hits, divided by innings pitched. Lower is better; under 1.00 is excellent.

gb.name: Ground Ball Rate
gb.definition: Percentage of batted balls hit on the ground. Ground balls rarely become home runs, so a higher rate usually helps a pitcher.

fb_velocity.name: Fastball Velocity
fb_velocity.definition: Average speed of the pitcher's fastball.

extension.name: Extension
extension.definition: How far in front of the rubber the pitcher releases the ball. More extension makes a pitch look faster to the hitter.

percentile.name: Percentile Rank
percentile.definition: Where a player ranks against other MLB players in the same season, on a 0–100 scale. A 90th-percentile ranking means the player did better than about 90% of the players who had enough playing time to be ranked. Rankings are flipped where needed so a higher percentile is always better, even for stats like Strikeout Rate where hitters want a low number. SimpleSavant's category scores are averages of these percentiles.

avg.name: Batting Average (AVG)
avg.definition: Hits divided by at-bats. It shows how often a hitter gets a hit in an official at-bat. Walks, hit-by-pitches and sacrifices are not at-bats, so they do not change it.

obp.name: On-Base Percentage (OBP)
obp.definition: How often a hitter reaches base by a hit, walk or hit-by-pitch: (hits + walks + hit-by-pitches) ÷ (at-bats + walks + hit-by-pitches + sacrifice flies).

slg.name: Slugging Percentage (SLG)
slg.definition: Total bases divided by at-bats. A single counts as 1 base, a double 2, a triple 3 and a home run 4, so slugging rewards extra-base hits and power.

ops.name: On-Base Plus Slugging (OPS)
ops.definition: On-base percentage plus slugging percentage. It combines how often a hitter gets on base with how much power they hit for, in one number.

hr.name: Home Runs (HR)
hr.definition: Number of home runs the player hit in the season. It is a season total, so players with more games and plate appearances have more chances to hit them.

games.name: Games Played (G)
games.definition: Number of games the player appeared in during the season.
games.note: Playing-time stat: shows how much a player played, not how well

pa.name: Plate Appearances (PA)
pa.definition: Every completed turn at the plate, including walks, hit-by-pitches and sacrifices. Rate stats such as AVG and K% are more reliable when they come from more plate appearances.
pa.note: Playing-time stat: shows how much a player played, not how well

ab.name: At-Bats (AB)
ab.definition: Plate appearances not counting walks, hit-by-pitches, sacrifice bunts, sacrifice flies or catcher's interference. Batting average and slugging are calculated per at-bat.
ab.note: Playing-time stat: shows how much a player played, not how well

hits.name: Hits (H)
hits.definition: Times the batter reached base safely on a ball they hit, without help from an error or a fielder's choice: singles, doubles, triples and home runs.

doubles.name: Doubles (2B)
doubles.definition: Hits on which the batter safely reached second base.

triples.name: Triples (3B)
triples.definition: Hits on which the batter safely reached third base. Triples are rare and usually need speed as well as a well-hit ball.

runs.name: Runs (R)
runs.definition: Times the player crossed home plate to score. It also depends on teammates driving the player in.

rbi.name: Runs Batted In (RBI)
rbi.definition: Runs that scored because of the batter's plate appearance, such as on a hit, a sacrifice fly or a bases-loaded walk. It depends heavily on how often teammates are on base.

sb.name: Stolen Bases (SB)
sb.definition: Times the runner safely took the next base on their own, usually by running while the pitch is thrown, without the help of a hit, walk or error.

strikeouts.name: Strikeouts (K)
strikeouts.definition: Plate appearances that end with a third strike. For hitters it is how many times they struck out, so fewer is better. For pitchers it is how many batters they struck out, so more is better.

walks.name: Walks (BB)
walks.definition: Plate appearances where the batter is awarded first base on four balls (pitches outside the strike zone that they did not swing at). For hitters more is better; for pitchers fewer is better.

ip.name: Innings Pitched (IP)
ip.definition: Outs the pitcher recorded, divided by 3. The digit after the decimal counts extra outs, not tenths: 195.1 means 195⅓ innings and 195.2 means 195⅔.
ip.note: Workload stat: shows how much a pitcher pitched, not how well

g_gs.name: Games / Games Started (G / GS)
g_gs.definition: Games the pitcher appeared in, and how many of those they started. Mostly starts means a starting pitcher; few or no starts means a relief pitcher.
g_gs.note: Role stat: shows whether the pitcher starts games or comes in from the bullpen

wl.name: Wins – Losses (W–L)
wl.definition: Games the pitcher was credited with winning or charged with losing. A starter usually needs to pitch at least 5 innings with the lead to earn a win. Because wins depend on how many runs teammates score, the record is a weak measure of how well the pitcher actually pitched.
wl.note: Team-dependent stat: read it alongside ERA and WHIP

saves.name: Saves (SV)
saves.definition: Credited to the relief pitcher who finishes a game their team wins while protecting a close lead, usually entering with a lead of 3 runs or fewer. Starting pitchers almost never get saves, so a low number is not a weakness for them.
saves.note: Role stat: mostly earned by closers

k9.name: Strikeouts per 9 Innings (K/9)
k9.definition: Strikeouts × 9 ÷ innings pitched: about how many batters the pitcher would strike out over a full nine-inning game.

bb9.name: Walks per 9 Innings (BB/9)
bb9.definition: Walks × 9 ÷ innings pitched: about how many batters the pitcher would walk over a full nine-inning game. Lower means better control.

kbb.name: Strikeout-to-Walk Ratio (K/BB)
kbb.definition: Strikeouts divided by walks. Higher means the pitcher strikes batters out often while rarely walking them.

hits_allowed.name: Hits Allowed (H)
hits_allowed.definition: Hits opposing batters got against the pitcher. Fewer is better, but read it next to Innings Pitched: pitchers who throw more innings allow more hits.

hr_allowed.name: Home Runs Allowed (HR)
hr_allowed.definition: Home runs opposing batters hit against the pitcher. Fewer is better, but read it next to Innings Pitched.

opp_avg.name: Opponent Batting Average (AVG against)
opp_avg.definition: The batting average of hitters facing this pitcher: hits allowed ÷ at-bats against.
